open_points.subject: Authorization check ownership
open_points.text:
any check other than the request forms it reads by their models and the single `Authorization` field in
  the Bearer scheme its extractor reads, or any delivery rule;
open_points.question: Does `deliverer_router` own the complete A5 rule 1 authentication check, and, if not, which module owns each part of checking header multiplicity, the Bearer syntax and the constant-time token comparison?
options: `deliverer_router` owns every check in A5 rule 1
`deliverer_router` checks only the field count and Bearer syntax while another module compares the token
`deliverer_router` only reads an extractor result and `http_router_backend` or another module owns the checks
open_points.default_guess: Make `deliverer_router` own every check in A5 rule 1 because it receives the token and must enforce the check before identifiers and bodies.

open_points.subject: Authorization knowledge required by deliverer_router
open_points.text:
the routes, their operations, the order of A5 rule 1 (the token before the identifiers and the body), the
  request form of A3 rule 4 and the `photo_id` form of A4 rule 2.
open_points.question: If `deliverer_router` performs the newly permitted Authorization check, must it know all of A5 rule 1—including duplicate-field rejection, case-insensitive scheme comparison, exact spacing and constant-time token comparison—or only the stated ordering rule?
options: Add all of A5 rule 1 to what `deliverer_router` knows
Keep only the ordering knowledge and give the authentication semantics to the extractor's owning module
Define a separate authentication contract that `deliverer_router` may know
open_points.default_guess: Add all of A5 rule 1 to what `deliverer_router` knows.

open_points.subject: Authorization extractor boundary
open_points.text:
the reading of the single
  `Authorization` field in the Bearer scheme by the extractor the backend emits
open_points.question: What does the extractor emitted by `http_router_backend` return to `deliverer_router`, and does it merely expose every raw Authorization field or itself reject missing, duplicate, malformed or non-Bearer fields?
options: It exposes all raw Authorization field occurrences and `deliverer_router` decides every refusal
It validates field multiplicity and Bearer syntax but leaves token comparison to `deliverer_router`
It performs the complete authentication check and returns an authenticated token result
open_points.default_guess: Have it expose all raw field occurrences without producing an HTTP refusal, so `deliverer_router` can apply A5 rule 1 and route every refusal through `refusal_answer`.
